name: Pans & Kitchen Tools
summary: Caring for cast iron, nonstick and stainless pans, and the handful of tools worth having.

sections.heading: Caring for pans
blocks: Which pan suits which job is in [Stovetop Cooking](guide:stovetop#pans). Caring for each:

items: **Cast iron**: wash with hot water and a brush or a little soap (modern soap won't strip seasoning), dry it on the burner, and rub in a few drops of oil while it's warm. Never soak it. If it rusts, scrub the rust off, then oil it and bake it upside down at 450°F (230°C) for an hour.
**Stainless steel**: dishwasher-safe. For stuck-on bits, simmer a little water in the pan and scrape; a paste of Bar Keepers Friend or baking soda removes stains.
**Nonstick**: medium heat or below, never preheated empty on high. Use wood or silicone tools and wash by hand with a soft sponge. Replace it when the coating scratches or flakes.
**Enameled cast iron**: don't heat it empty on high or plunge it hot into cold water, which can crack the enamel. Soak to loosen stuck food.

sections.heading: Tools worth having

items: **An instant-read thermometer**: the single biggest step up for cooking meat. See the [doneness chart](guide:doneness-and-food-safety#doneness-chart).
**A kitchen scale**: more accurate than cups for baking, and fewer dishes.
**Sheet pans** (rimmed half-sheet pans, 18×13 inches (46×33 cm)): roasting, baking, everything.
**A large cutting board** that doesn't slide, and a separate one for raw meat.
**Tongs, a flat spatula (fish spatula) and a wooden spoon.**
**A Dutch oven**: soups, braises, bread, deep-frying.
**A big pot** for pasta and stock, and a medium saucepan with a lid for grains and sauces.
**Measuring cups and spoons, a whisk, a colander, and a microplane** for zest, garlic and hard cheese.
